title: The wave that was not water
style: documentary photograph, 1919, winter, available light, muted colour, fine grain, no text, no watermark, no modern objects
negative: text, letters, words, watermark, logo, cartoon, cgi, painting, illustration, modern objects, cars

lines.vo: In January 1919 a steel tank in Boston's North End burst.
lines.image: a winter street of brick warehouses under a low grey sky
pieces: steel storage tank above a wharf

shot.signature: one slow push straight into the tank until its riveted seam is the whole frame — the shot exists to make you look at the thing before it fails

lines.vo: Two million gallons of molasses ran down Commercial Street.
lines.image: a narrow cobbled street between brick buildings
pieces: wooden barrel lying on its side

shot.signature: the camera falls back down the street as if pushed, opening the frame instead of closing it — the only shot in the reel that retreats

lines.vo: The wave stood fifteen feet high and moved at thirty-five miles an hour.
lines.image: a dark warehouse wall lit from one side

shot.signature: the number arrives alone on the card and everything else in the reel stops for it — no photograph, no prop, nothing to look at but the height

lines.vo: It tore a firehouse off its foundation and buried the horses.
lines.image: a wrecked wooden building leaning into black mud

shot.signature: a hard fast push onto the leaning wall, harder than any other shot, so the cut lands like the building did

lines.vo: Twenty-one people drowned in it and a hundred and fifty were hurt.
lines.image: a long hall of empty iron cots

shot.signature: the count is pinned up rather than spoken over a picture — the shot stops being a place and becomes a record

lines.vo: The company paid six hundred thousand dollars and blamed anarchists.
lines.image: a wooden courtroom bench in low light

shot.signature: the camera pulls off the bench while the front page settles over it — the reel ends by backing away from the room
